Q: Add title row with ARRAYFORMULA in Google Sheets A:

the if(row(A:A) = 1, "spent" technique of printing headers is a bad practice from the old, old era with no benefit at all (frankly, it should be banned by AGSB - Association of Google Sheets Bros)

nowadays we have modern VSTACK and HSTACK that fully replace array { } syntax and go one step further:

  • they are able to join 2+ arrays of different sizes without throwing any ARRAY_ERROR

  • also, they are able to read any errors that are from down the line

  • they can take null range outputting empty row or column

  • and the last benefit is, that there is no need of using custom/incompatible (locale specific) delimiters (, ; vs \ ;) to guide the flow of stacking

therefore, the simplest:

=VSTACK("spent"; INDEX(B2:B - A2:A))

VSTACK for vertical stacking, INDEX as array enabler (as it is shorter to type than ARRAYFORMULA)

furthermore, for restricting the spillage of arrayformula into empty rows most people does the outdated if(len(A2:A), or if(A2:A="",, which is not very efficient. instead use compound range where last row is determined by

XMATCH(;-(A:A="");;-1)

that will do in 99.999% of cases. but if you wish for 100% then use slightly longer:

XMATCH(;-ISBLANK(A:A);;-1)

and also, to not repeat ranges (or any stuff) use hyper-efficient LET where you can set variables so the formula could go like this:

=VSTACK("spent"; LET(
 x; XMATCH(;(A:A="")*(B:B="");;-1);
 a; A2:INDEX(A:A; x);
 b; B2:INDEX(B:B; x);
 b-a))

or if array has no empty cells in between:

=VSTACK("spent"; INDEX(TOCOL(B2:B; 1)-TOCOL(A2:A; 1)))

Q: Does podman-compose support build-time volumes? If so, what is the syntax? A:

podman-compose defines its capabilities in terms of the Compose specification, and the build: block doesn't allow volumes:. In the implementation, the function that generates podman build arguments doesn't look for a volumes: key and doesn't generate a -v option. This doesn't appear to be a supported option via Podman Compose.

While podman build does support a -v option, to the extent that Podman commands mirror the equivalent Docker commands, docker build does not support a -v option, and I might not rely on this capability.

The Containerfile (and Dockerfile) RUN command supports a per-command RUN --mount option which has most of the capabilities you could need from a global volume mount, including mounting parts of the host filesystem (read-only) or having a persistent build cache. I'd prefer this as an option with more mainstream support. For example,

RUN --mount=type=bind,source=build,target=/host-build \
  cp -a /host-build/dist /app/dist

Q: can 7zZip compress non encrypting and without random salt? A:

7-Zip no usa sal aleatoria cuando no hay cifrado. Si comprimes archivos sin activar el cifrado, no existe ningún proceso criptográfico que cambie el resultado. La razón por la que los archivos .7z cambian aunque el contenido sea igual es porque el archivo comprimido guarda metadatos, como fechas de modificación, acceso o creación, y a veces el orden de los archivos dentro del contenedor. Esos datos pueden variar cada vez que se crea el archivo, produciendo un hash diferente. Para reducir esto, puedes desactivar los timestamps con -mtc=off -mtm=off -mta=off o usar tar para crear un archivo determinista antes de comprimirlo con 7-Zip.

Q: Modify a bar plot into a staked plot keeping the original values A:
  • Using the level keyword in DataFrame and Series aggregations, df.sum(axis=1,level=[0]), is deprecated.
    • Use df.groupby(level=0, axis=1).sum()
  • df.div(dfg).mul(100).round(1).astype(str) creates a DataFrame of strings with the 'Female' and 'Male' percent for each of the 'Skills', which can be used to create a custom bar label.
  • As shown in this answer, use matplotlib.pyplot.bar_label to annotate the bars, which has a labels= parameter for custom labels.
  • Tested in python 3.11, pandas 1.5.3, matplotlib 3.7.0, seaborn 0.12.2
# group df to create the bar plot
dfg = df.groupby(level=0, axis=1).sum()

# calculate the Female / Male percent for each Skill
percent_s = df.div(dfg).mul(100).round(1).astype(str)

# plot the bars
ax = dfg.plot(kind='bar', figsize=(10, 7), rot=0, width=0.9, ylabel='Total Percent\n(Female/Male split)')

# iterate through the bar containers
for c in ax.containers:
    # get the Skill label
    label = c.get_label()
    # use the Skill label to get the current group based on level, join the strings,and get an array of custom labels
    labels = percent_s.loc[:, percent_s.columns.get_level_values(0).isin([label])].agg('/'.join, axis=1).values
    # add the custom labels to the center of the bars
    ax.bar_label(c, labels=labels, label_type='center')
    # add total percent to the top of the bars
    ax.bar_label(c, weight='bold', fmt='%g%%')

percent_s

Skills     Above basic        Basic          Low      
Gender          Female  Male Female  Male Female  Male
Math              50.0  50.0   50.0  50.0   50.0  50.0
Literature        50.0  50.0   40.0  60.0   33.3  66.7
Physics           48.0  52.0   47.6  52.4   55.2  44.8
  • Optionally, melt df into a long form, and use sns.catplot with kind='bar' to plot each 'Gender' in a separate Facet.
# melt df into a long form
dfm = df.melt(ignore_index=False).reset_index(names='Subject')

# plot the melted dataframe
g = sns.catplot(kind='bar', data=dfm, x='Subject', y='value', col='Gender', hue='Skills')

# Flatten the axes for ease of use
axes = g.axes.ravel()

# relabel the yaxis
axes[0].set_ylabel('Percent')

# add bar labels
for ax in axes:
    for c in ax.containers:
        ax.bar_label(c, fmt='%0.1f%%')

  • Or swap x= and col= to col='Subject' and x='Gender'.

Q: Could not load file or assembly 'System.Windows.Forms... ' exception A:

I received a similar error message attempting to get this application to run on a Linux box using Mono:

$ mono CertViewer.exe 

Unhandled Exception:
System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Could not load file or assembly 'System.Windows.Forms, Version=4.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b77a5c561934e089' or one of its dependencies.
File name: 'System.Windows.Forms, Version=4.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b77a5c561934e089'
[ERROR] FATAL UNHANDLED EXCEPTION: System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Could not load file or assembly 'System.Windows.Forms, Version=4.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b77a5c561934e089' or one of its dependencies.
File name: 'System.Windows.Forms, Version=4.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b77a5c561934e089'

The solution in my case was to install the libmono-system-windows-forms4.0-cil package from the Ubuntu repositories, including dependencies recommended by the package system.

I don't claim to understand the circumstances described in the original question. I post this in hopes of helping someone not too familiar with Mono/.NET (like me) to locate the solution for this missing library, since this SO question ranks high in web search results for could not load file or assembly System.Windows.Forms.

Q: Why ORA-03106 in an OCI program when SELECTing more than 1 row? 10g only, not 11g A:

What exact version of Oracle client and server are in use?

There's a possible match on at least one known Oracle bug:

Applies to: Oracle Server - Enterprise Edition - Version: 10.2.0.1 to 10.2.0.2 - Release: 10.2 to 10.2 Information in this document applies to any platform. Checked for relevance on 21-Jan-2010

Symptoms OCI based application intermittently throws ORA-03106: fatal two-task communication proto error and has error entries in application log.

Important : The error may not bee seen in the alert.log and in the SQL NET trace files

Cause This has been identified as a Bug 4523125

Solution Upgrade the Client and the Server to 10.2.0.3

More generally, this seems like an issue for Oracle Support.
